description: Renovate opens bump PRs into the existing branch→PR→merge→git-pull-on-box deploy flow. See docs/APP_UPDATES.md. Auto-merge is deliberately OFF everywhere: this stack holds members' photos and passwords — a human reviews every bump, and deploy to the box is a separate manual step.

prConcurrentLimit WAS 5, AND IT STARVED THE ONE DEPENDENCY THAT HAD NO OTHER NOTIFICATION PATH. Measured 2026-10-14: five open Renovate PRs (#26, #30, #32, #70, #72 — three of them since July) held every slot, so Renovate had never opened an Ollama PR for any version, while host/mac-mini/versions.env pinned 0.33.3 and upstream was 0.40.x. The custom manager below was working the whole time; the dashboard (issue #27) listed ollama/ollama under Rate-Limited. Nothing was broken, the queue was just full of trivial base-image bumps nobody had reviewed. Raising this to 10 (Renovate's own default) is a MITIGATION, not a fix — the cap saturates again at 10 unreviewed PRs. The fix is that the mini's runtime no longer depends on a PR to be noticed: see docs/MAC_MINI.md.

The concurrent PR limit is enforced PER REPOSITORY. A packageRules entry may carry prConcurrentLimit and the schema accepts it, but it cannot reserve a slot — the only documented nested budget is vulnerabilityAlerts, which Renovate's docs say gets its own on top of the repo-wide one. There is no way to exempt the mac-mini label from this cap.

customManagers.description: The Mac mini's runtime version pins. They are shell-style assignments in host/mac-mini/versions.env, not image tags in a compose file, so Renovate needs to be told where to look. GENERALISED from OLLAMA_VERSION to any <NAME>_VERSION when oMLX was added, rather than adding a second near-identical manager: one regex to keep working is better than two that can drift apart. The `# renovate:` comment above each pin is still load-bearing — it carries the datasource and package name — so don't reformat that file without re-checking this matches. NO versioningTemplate here on purpose: the two pins need different schemes (ollama/ollama is semver, jundot/omlx ships pep440 'rc' tags as its current release), so each is set in its own packageRule rather than having one template silently impose semver on both.

packageRules.description: Matrix identity plane. Synapse and MAS hold accounts, sessions and the server's federation identity, and MAS bumps have historically carried DB migrations — same care as the other stateful services. Element is just a static webapp but is versioned alongside them.

MAS tags have NO leading v (1.23.0), unlike synapse and element-web (v1.159.0) right beside them. Without this, Renovate reads the versions as a different scheme and either goes quiet or proposes nonsense.

description: Ollama on the Mac mini. Applying a bump replaces /Applications/Ollama.app on a running host, so it is never automatic — `host/mac-mini/install.sh --upgrade-ollama` is the act. Low stakes though: the mini is AI-chat-only, nothing else depends on it (HARDWARE_FAILURE.md).

prPriority 10 puts this first in the queue of updates AWAITING CREATION, ahead of the stateful rule's 5 and every unprioritised container bump. Note what that does and does not do: prPriority only SORTS. It cannot evict a PR that already exists, so it did nothing at all while five open PRs held the cap — it decides who takes the next slot that frees, not who gets one now. Ranked first not because this is the most important dependency (it is the least — see the risk inversion in docs/MAC_MINI.md) but because it is the scarcest-notified: everything else here is a container image the drift monitor and the box's own tags also account for.

oMLX on the Mac mini — the MLX inference server that now holds the primary model. Applying a bump replaces an application bundle on the host that serves the household's chat, so it is never automatic: `host/mac-mini/install.sh --install-omlx` is the act, and the reconcile reports the skew meanwhile. Same low stakes as Ollama beside it (HARDWARE_FAILURE.md: AI chat only, nothing else depends on it).

AN 'rc' TAG IS THIS PROJECT'S CURRENT RELEASE. Measured 2026-10-16: GitHub's releases/latest returns v0.7.1rc1 with prerelease=false and draft=false, and the project's homepage download button points at releases/latest. So rc builds are the release train, not something to filter out.

THIS RULE PREVIOUSLY GOT THAT BACKWARDS, and the failure would have been silent. It used `versioning: semver` plus ignoreUnstable to exclude 'unstable' tags, on the reading that prerelease=false on an rc tag was upstream mislabelling. But '0.7.1rc1' is not valid semver, so Renovate could not parse it and skipped it — which does not mean 'wait for a stable release', it means this dependency goes quiet and host/mac-mini/versions.env sits on an old pin while every check reports green. That is the same shape as the four months this repo spent not hearing about Ollama, arrived at from the opposite direction.

pep440 understands '0.7.1rc1' as a prerelease of 0.7.1, so the pin can track the release train. ignoreUnstable is therefore OFF — with it on, pep440 would correctly identify rc tags as prereleases and skip exactly the releases we want. allowedVersions excludes .dev builds instead, which are genuine between-release snapshots (v0.7.1.dev1 and .dev2 both also report prerelease=false, so the GitHub flag cannot make this distinction either).

minimumReleaseAge 7 days rather than the repo-wide 3. This project ships frequently and a regression lands on the one service members notice immediately; a week of other people's bug reports is cheap insurance. It also keeps a fast-moving dependency from eating slots in a PR cap this repo has already been starved by once.

packageRules.description: Stateful / identity-critical services: never batch, call them out loudly. A bad update here is a trust event — read the release notes before merging, snapshot/backup before deploying.

Ente ships only a rolling `latest` (no version tags), so it's pinned by digest in compose. Enable digest pinning/updates so Renovate PRs when latest's digest moves; it's the service holding the photos, so every bump is a deliberate, read-the-notes event.
Postgres: major upgrades require a dump/restore migration, not a tag bump. Only take minor/patch within 15.x.
Jellyfin: track stable only — no release candidates (memory: 12.0-rc explicitly rejected).
Vaultwarden fork (timshel/oidcwarden) uses vYYYY.M.P-N tags; loose versioning so Renovate can order them.

description: Python images: HOLD BELOW 3.13. Measured 2026-10-15 by building both music images on 3.14 — services/music/Dockerfile (beets 2.12.0) builds fine, but services/music/Dockerfile.poll (streamrip 2.1.0) FAILS: streamrip pins a Pillow with no cp314 wheel, so pip builds it from source and slim-bookworm carries no C headers to do that with. Loud at build time rather than silent at runtime, but it would block any rebuild of the Qobuz poller.

Fixes considered and rejected. Adding gcc/libjpeg-dev/zlib1g-dev bloats an image whose only job is extracting Qobuz's app_id/secret via QobuzSpoofer. Bumping streamrip abandons the version validated end-to-end on 2026-07-15 (its login is broken upstream — Qobuz #954/#956 — and only QobuzSpoofer is reused). Splitting the two files onto different Pythons works but leaves a divergence Renovate re-proposes forever and a human re-decides every time. Nothing needs 3.14 and 3.12 is supported into 2028, so both stay put.
LIFT THIS when streamrip's dependency tree carries a cp314 Pillow. Closed PR #30 is the record.

qbittorrent: ignore anything from 6.x up. The dependency dashboard offered 'linuxserver/qbittorrent 5.2.4 -> 20.04.1' on 2026-10-15. 20.04.1 is not a qBittorrent version — it is an Ubuntu release number, and the real tag list for this image tops out at 5.2.4, which is what we already run. Renovate is mis-sorting one of linuxserver's compound tags (5.2.4_v2.0.15-ls480 and friends) into a plausible-looking semver.

Merging that would have pinned a tag that does not exist and broken the deploy at pull time. The cap <6 keeps real 5.x patches flowing while excluding the phantom. Revisit if qBittorrent ever genuinely reaches 6.x.
